content.title: SpaceX to Launch 25 Starlink Satellites from Vandenberg on Sunday - edhat
content.text: Submit News Subscribe Donate SUBSCRIBE Search SpaceX (courtesy) SHARE UPDATE: This launch was rescheduled for Monday, April 6, 2026, and successfully took place at 7:50 p.m. Read the updated story here. The U.S. Space Force has cleared SpaceX to launch a Falcon 9 carrying the Starlink 17-35 mission on Sunday, April 5, 2026, during a window from 4:03 p.m. to 8:03 p.m. PT from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E). Edhat-2 Next In: 15s Watch SpaceX says the mission will deploy 25 Starlink satellites to low-Earth orbit. The first-stage booster flying this mission is making its debut and is slated to land on the droneship “Of Course I Still Love You,” stationed in the Pacific Ocean. A live webcast will begin about five minutes before liftoff at https://www.spacex.com/launches/sl-17-35, on X @SpaceX, and via the X TV app. Residents in Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may hear one or more sonic booms during the launch, depending on weather and other conditions, according to officials. Vandenberg SFB highlighted its role as a critical national security spaceport, enabling assured access to space and supporting missions that include nuclear deterrence, homeland defense, global command and control of space assets, orbital tracking, and training for space operations Guardians and nuclear Airmen.
